name: Document Processing Workflow
description: End-to-end document processing pipeline where customers send CSV/Excel files through validation, mapping, AI classification, quality checks, and final output generation. Demonstrates parallel processing branches with condition gates, human-in-the-loop reviews, and a linear fix path for rejected data.
purpose: Automate the complete document processing lifecycle: receive customer CSV/Excel files, create a case record, upload files, run parallel order matching / field mapping / document classification, merge results, run the data pipeline, handle rejections via human fix, and produce the final CV output.

wrapperProps.label: File Name
wrapperProps.description: Name of the uploaded CSV/Excel file.

wrapperProps.label: File Type
wrapperProps.description: Type of file: csv or excel.

__comment_node_definitions: NodeDefinition templates that business nodes reference. Created via POST /node-definitions and stored separately. Included here for documentation.

node_definitions.name: Create CV Record
node_definitions.description: Business node: creates an initial case/CV record for the incoming document processing request.

node_definitions.name: Upload File
node_definitions.description: Business node: uploads the customer CSV/Excel file to the file service for downstream processing.

node_definitions.name: Create Order with History Matching
node_definitions.description: Business node: matches incoming data rows against historical orders. User reviews/edits matching results before confirming.

node_definitions.name: Create Field Mapping
node_definitions.description: Business node: maps incoming file columns to target schema fields. User reviews and confirms field mappings before proceeding.

node_definitions.name: Classify/Identify Documents
node_definitions.description: Business node: uses AI to classify and identify document types and content categories from the uploaded file.

node_definitions.name: Handle Document Rejection
node_definitions.description: Business node: processes rejected documents — logs rejection reason and notifies stakeholders.

node_definitions.name: Run Data Block Pipeline
node_definitions.description: Business node: executes the data processing pipeline combining matched orders, field mappings, and classifications. User reviews pipeline input before execution.

node_definitions.name: Create Final CV
node_definitions.description: Business node: generates the final CV output document from the processed data. Data remains viewable after dispatch for auditing.

__comment_parameters: Nodes use a unified 'parameters' field. The backend splits it into engine-internal 'config' (behavior rules) and 'input_binding' (data mappings) based on node type. The frontend never needs to know this distinction.

nodes.name: Customer Sends File
nodes.description: Starts when a customer sends a CSV/Excel file for processing.
nodes.instruction: Listen on the 'documents.submitted' event topic. When an event arrives, extract the trigger_payload containing customer_id, file_name, and file_type.

nodes.name: Create CV Record
nodes.description: BUSINESS NODE (json, auto-dispatch): Creates an initial case/CV record for the document processing request.
nodes.instruction: Create a new CV record using customer_id and file_name from the trigger payload. The response contains the cv_id used by all downstream nodes.

nodes.name: Upload File
nodes.description: BUSINESS NODE (csv_multi, auto-dispatch): Uploads the customer CSV/Excel file to the file service.
nodes.instruction: Upload the file using the cv_id from the previous step and file metadata from the trigger. The response contains file_id for downstream processing.

nodes.name: Parallel Processing
nodes.description: Fan-out into three parallel branches: order matching, field mapping, and document classification.
nodes.instruction: Fork into three concurrent branches. All three must complete before merging. Fail fast on any failure.

nodes.name: Order Matching
nodes.description: BUSINESS NODE (csv_multi + before_dispatch HITL): Matches incoming data rows against historical orders. Workflow pauses for user review.
nodes.instruction: Match file data against historical orders. The CSV data grid is presented to the user for review/edit. On Confirm, the matched orders are dispatched to the HTTP worker.

nodes.name: Mapping Auto-Confirmed?
nodes.description: Checks whether the order matching was auto-confirmed (high confidence) or needs human review.
nodes.instruction: Evaluate whether match_confidence exceeds the auto-confirm threshold. If true, proceed directly to merge. If false, route through human confirmation.

nodes.name: Confirm Mapping
nodes.description: Pauses workflow for a human to review and confirm the order matching results.
nodes.instruction: Present the order matching results to a business user. They review the matched orders and either confirm or reject the mapping. On confirm, proceed to merge.

parameters.message: Please review and confirm the order matching results for CV {{$create-cv.output.cv_id}}.

nodes.name: Field Mapping
nodes.description: BUSINESS NODE (csv_multi + before_dispatch HITL): Maps incoming file columns to target schema fields. Workflow pauses for user review.
nodes.instruction: Analyze the uploaded file columns and propose field mappings. The CSV data grid shows source-to-target column mappings. User reviews, adjusts mappings, and confirms.

nodes.name: Confirm Field Mapping
nodes.description: Pauses workflow for a human to review and confirm the field mapping results.
nodes.instruction: Present the field mapping results to a business user. They review source-to-target mappings and either confirm or request changes.

parameters.message: Please review and confirm the field mappings for CV {{$create-cv.output.cv_id}}.

nodes.name: Classify Documents
nodes.description: BUSINESS NODE (csv_multi, auto-dispatch): Uses AI to classify and identify document types from the uploaded file.
nodes.instruction: Send the file to the AI classification service. The response contains document type classifications and confidence scores.

nodes.name: AI Processing
nodes.description: Processes classifications through additional AI quality checks and enrichment.
nodes.instruction: Run additional AI-based quality checks on the classified documents. Validates classification confidence and enriches with metadata.

nodes.name: Documents Rejected?
nodes.description: Checks whether any documents were rejected by the AI classification/processing step.
nodes.instruction: Evaluate whether the AI processing flagged any documents for rejection. If rejected, route to rejection handling. Otherwise, proceed to merge.

nodes.name: Handle Rejection
nodes.description: BUSINESS NODE (json, auto-dispatch): Processes rejected documents — logs rejection reason and notifies stakeholders.
nodes.instruction: Log the rejection details, notify the customer, and record the rejection reason in the CV record.

nodes.name: Merge Parallel Branches
nodes.description: Waits for all three parallel branches (matching, mapping, classification) to complete.
nodes.instruction: Converge the three parallel branches. Uses wait_all — all three branches must complete before proceeding to the pipeline.

nodes.name: Run Data Pipeline
nodes.description: BUSINESS NODE (csv_multi + before_dispatch HITL): Runs the data processing pipeline combining all three branch results. User reviews pipeline input before execution.
nodes.instruction: Combine matched orders, field mappings, and classifications into a single pipeline run. The CSV data grid shows the combined data. User reviews and confirms before the pipeline executes.

nodes.name: Any Rejections?
nodes.description: Checks whether the pipeline produced any rejected data blocks that need fixing.
nodes.instruction: Evaluate whether the pipeline result contains rejections. If yes, route through the fix-data path. If no, proceed directly to merge.

nodes.name: Fix Rejected Data
nodes.description: Pauses workflow for a human to fix rejected data blocks before re-running the pipeline.
nodes.instruction: Present the rejected data blocks to a business user. They review the issues, fix the data, and confirm to re-run the pipeline.

parameters.message: Some data blocks were rejected in the pipeline for CV {{$create-cv.output.cv_id}}. Please review and fix the rejected data.

nodes.name: Re-run Pipeline
nodes.description: Re-runs the data pipeline after the human has fixed the rejected data.
nodes.instruction: Re-execute the data pipeline with the corrected data. Uses the same pipeline endpoint but with updated/fixed input.

nodes.name: Merge Pipeline Paths
nodes.description: Merges the direct (no rejection) and fix (rejection → re-run) paths.
nodes.instruction: Converge the two paths from the rejection condition. Uses wait_any — only one path is ever active.

nodes.name: Final Approval
nodes.description: Pauses workflow for final human approval before generating the final CV output.
nodes.instruction: Present the complete processed data to a business user for final review and approval before creating the final CV document.

parameters.message: Please review the complete processed data for CV {{$create-cv.output.cv_id}} and approve for final CV generation.

nodes.name: Create Final CV
nodes.description: BUSINESS NODE (csv_multi + after_dispatch): Generates the final CV output document. Dispatches immediately but data remains viewable for auditing.
nodes.instruction: Generate the final CV document from the processed and approved data. The after_dispatch edit_mode means the data grid remains viewable in the run view for auditing purposes.

notes.parameters_convention: All nodes use a single 'parameters' field. The backend splits it into engine-internal 'config' (behavior/control-flow rules) and 'input_binding' (data mappings from upstream nodes) based on node type. The frontend never needs to know this distinction.
notes.worker_id_convention: worker_id uses worker_type (e.g. 'http-request-worker') as the stable routing identifier. The worker-executor resolves worker_type to the current registration.
notes.dag_constraint: No cycles allowed — the DAG validator enforces acyclicity via topological sort. The 'fix data → rerun pipeline' loop from the BPMN diagram is modeled as a linear fix path with a MERGE (wait_any) to rejoin the main flow.

data_mode_examples.json: create-cv, handle-rejection — standard JSON passthrough, no CSV conversion
data_mode_examples.csv_multi: upload-file, order-matching, field-mapping, classify-docs, run-pipeline, create-final-cv — multi-row CSV with editable data grid

edit_mode_examples.none: create-cv, upload-file, classify-docs, handle-rejection — auto-dispatch, no user interaction
edit_mode_examples.before_dispatch: order-matching, field-mapping, run-pipeline — workflow pauses (PENDING_INPUT), user reviews/edits CSV data grid, confirms to dispatch
edit_mode_examples.after_dispatch: create-final-cv — dispatches immediately, but CSV remains editable in run view for auditing
